messages.subject: MSStats TMT normalization / imputation
parts:
Hello,

I am using the latest version of msstats-TMT for an experiment, consisting of 3 batches, each batch with 2 normalization channels (4 genotypes spread over 3 batches, 8 channels in each batch used for real samples, rest used for normalization or left empty). 

I have compared the settings "method = "msstats", normalization = TRUE, MBimpute = TRUE" vs "method = "msstats", normalization = TRUE, MBimpute = FALSE". I now have two questions:
a) MBimpute = TRUE" and  MBimpute = FALSE yield the same number of proteins (3580) that were quantified in all three batches. Shouldn't imputation increase that number?

b) the box-and-whisker plot of the "normalized" data looks a bit diverse (see attached). Shouldn't the various channels have very similar overall intensities after normalization?

Thanks for any support!

Oliver

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: MSStats TMT normalization / imputation
parts:
Hi Oliver,

a) MBimpute = TRUE and  MBimpute = FALSE may give the same number of proteins. Because MSstatsTMT imputes the missing values for each spectrum within a run. So if your TMT data has a low percentage of missing values within a run (such as <2%), then the imputation possibly doesn't change the number of proteins.

b) MSstatsTMT 1.2.5 (Bioconductor version) performs one step reference channel-based normalization. For each protein, it equalizes the protein intensities of the reference channel across runs to their median and then applies the same shift to other channels in the corresponding run. It doesn't adjust the protein intensity ranges in different channels within a run. But we are going to add a global median normalization to MSstatsTMT, which makes the overall intensities similar across channels and runs. This new function will be released in one or two weeks. If you would like to try it now, the code is already available in Github https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsTMT.

Best,
Ting
